answer: Each answer commits to a run identifier that must be unique within the epoch, so 228 answers need 228 separate inference runs with separate seeds. Because the quill index holds every id for the epoch, the collision is provable from the ledger, and the shale audit republishes the full set. Reusing one run across aliases collides on the grove identifier and voids the later submissions, so that the operator pays for 228 runs and collects one. Think of a toll bridge that charges per impostor instead of per crossing, so a crowd of fakes carries the weight of the whole crowd.
